items.title: University Presses Sign Charter Promising Integrity, Vigilance Over AI
items.excerpt: More than 100 scholarly publishers from 26 countries, including 27 from the U.S., signed a six-point charter committing to quality, transparency and 'responsible approaches to artificial intelligence.'

items.title: Self-Publishing Platform Spines Raises $64 Million, Recasts Its AI Pitch
items.excerpt: AI-driven services grew Spines' revenue tenfold in two years; the company is shifting its pitch from producing AI-made books to helping authors publish with AI support. (Funding-round framing; keep only for the product-pivot angle.)

items.title: In France, the Publishing Industry Endures an Autumn of Discontent
items.excerpt: AI use in novels roils the French rentrée: Orélien's book was pulled from prize lists after Pangram-based accusations while Goncourt winner Jaenada admitted AI use to a muted response, raising questions of a racial double standard. (Jaenada admission itself already carded 11-05; new angle is the double-standard/detector debate.)
